function: Receive combining (signal estimation) in MIMO with distributionally robust linear combiners and kernel-ridge combiners fitted on pilot data, robust to pilot scarcity and model uncertainty (pp. 5, 9-10).
system: Point-to-point narrow-band MIMO, M=4 transmit and N=8 receive antennas, no RIS; 26 radio paths; SNR -10 dB; carrier frequency not stated (pp. 3, 11).
method: Distributionally robust estimation: closed-form diagonal-loading Wiener/Capon, SDP-based Wasserstein/F-norm Wiener, and supervised kernel ridge receivers trained on pilots; neural-network versions not implemented (pp. 5-11).
data_channel: Custom simulator: 26 paths (25 random scatterers), Tx at [0,0], Rx at [500 m, 450 m]; Gaussian signals, 10% impulse noise; QPSK in the supplement (pp. 11, 17).
test_conditions: Combiners fit on pilot blocks (10-100 pilots) and tested on 500 non-pilot symbols of the same simulated channel; 250 Monte-Carlo runs; no new scenario or configuration (pp. 11-12).
baselines: Non-learned: Wiener, Wiener-DL, Wiener-DR, Wiener-CE variants, Capon, Capon-DL, ZF; Kernel is the proposed kernel receiver without loading; no neural receiver implemented (pp. 11-12).
metrics: Test mean-squared estimation error (MSE) averaged over 250 Monte-Carlo episodes; training time; symbol error rate in the supplement (pp. 11-12, 17).
complexity: Training time averaged over 250 Monte-Carlo episodes per combiner (Tables I-VI, p. 12), e.g., Wiener-DR 3.16e+00 vs Wiener-DL 9.81e-06 at 10 pilots; units not stated.
openness: Source data and code on GitHub: https://github.com/Spratm-Asleaf/DRRC (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 11: "there exist 26 radio paths" from 25 uniformly random scatterers; a custom geometric simulator, with no 3GPP, COST 2100 or DeepMIMO model and no measured data mentioned.
q2_support: p. 4: "communication data are drawn from the same unknown distribution" as the pilots; p. 11: "The combiners are determined on the training data set" and tested on non-pilot data of the same frame, so no new scenario is tested.
q3_support: p. 11: "methods in Subsection V-B are not implemented in this section" (no earlier learned receiver compared); p. 11: "Kernel receiver (61) with ϵ0 = 0 in (60)" is the proposed kernel receiver without loading, an ablation. Non-learned baselines (Wiener, Capon, ZF) are present.
q4_support: p. 12: Table I note "The training time averaged on 250" Monte-Carlo episodes; Tables I-VI list a measured Time for every combiner, including the proposed Wiener-DR and Kernel-DL.
q5_support: p. 11: "All the source data and codes are available online at GitHub" with link https://github.com/Spratm-Asleaf/DRRC.
notes: Borderline on no_learning: the core is a closed-form or SDP distributionally robust design, and the only learned receivers are the kernel ridge ones (Kernel, Kernel-DL, pp. 9-10); neural-network receivers are only discussed (p. 11). Included because kernel regression fitted on pilots performs the combining and is the best receiver in Tables I-VI; reviewer to confirm that it counts as learned. Area 1: the output is the recovered transmit signal (p. 1, abstract); ISAC appears only as motivation. q4 rests on measured training times; the table does not give units.
